Japan Beats Growth Estimates in Tailwind for Rate Hikes
TOKYO--The Japanese economy grew at a slightly faster pace than initially estimated in the second quarter, reflecting a smaller contraction in corporate spending.
Real gross domestic product increased by an annualized 1.4% during the April-June period, compared with the preliminary estimate of 1.1% growth, revised government data showed Tuesday.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, the economy expanded 0.4%.
Capital expenditure led the revision, narrowing its decline to 0.9% from the previous quarter compared with the preliminary reading of a 1.2% drop.
Economists had widely anticipated the change after recent Ministry of Finance data showed business spending held up better than expected.
Meanwhile, private consumption was flat on quarter, unchanged from the preliminary report.
The growth print is another encouraging sign for the Bank of Japan as it considers an interest-rate increase at its upcoming meeting. Markets are now almost fully pricing in a September hike.

Policymakers have repeatedly said that they will examine the impact of Middle East tensions, foreign-exchange rate fluctuations, and demand related to artificial intelligence when considering the timing and pace of further policy action.
